07-253.r: Kelkar Task Forces (September 2002, Dr. Vijay L. Kelkar) → tax reform: simplify and rationalise direct and indirect taxes.

07-254.r: Kelkar Task Force on Direct Taxes → recommended removing tax rebate under Section 88 (also 80L and Section 10 interest income); final report December 2002.
07-254.t: Don't confuse Kelkar (direct-tax task force, 2002) with Chelliah, Shome or Rangarajan committees.

07-255.r: Latest tax reform committee → Kelkar Task Force (December 2002); Chelliah Committee 1991 (tax); Narasimhan 1991, 1998 (banking); Vaghul 1987 (call money market).
07-255.t: Narasimhan and Vaghul committees are banking and money market, not tax.

07-257.r: 1990s tax reforms → Tax Reforms Committee under Raja J. Chelliah (1991), covering direct and indirect taxes; made direct taxes the major tax revenue component.

07-259.r: No income tax relief → Indira Vikas Patra; NSC, PPF and National Savings Scheme gave income tax rebate.
07-259.h: 'Vikas Patra' (Indira or Kisan) → no tax benefit.

07-260.r: No income tax rebate → Kisan Vikas Patra; NSC, PPF and ULIP give investment plus tax deduction.
07-260.h: 'Vikas Patra' (Kisan or Indira) → no tax benefit.

07-261.r: PAN: 10-character alphanumeric ID; first five letters, next four numbers, last a letter; fourth character 'P' → Person (Individual).

07-262.r: PAN card is not proof of address (address not printed); it shows name, father's name, date of birth and PAN.

07-263.r: 2001 → PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee announced five-year excise duty holiday for industries in earthquake-hit Kutch district, Gujarat.

07-264.r: Union Budget 1999-2000 (FM Yashwant Sinha) → 10-year tax holiday for industries in the North-Eastern Region.

07-265.r: Panchayat finance sources → Finance Commission grant, central cooperative bank help, Centrally Sponsored Scheme allocations, State Finance Commission; NABARD not counted.

07-266.r: Gram Panchayat levies tax on local fairs; sales tax and land revenue are not Gram Panchayat taxes.

07-267.r: Fiscal stimulus in recession → cut tax rates and raise government spending; abolishing subsidies is not part of it.

07-268.r: NHAI (NHAI Act, 1988) → main fund source is cess; also capital base support, additional budgetary support, capital grant.

08-001.r: Economic and Social Planning → Concurrent List (List-3), Seventh Schedule; both Union and States can legislate.

08-002.r: DMEO → attached office of NITI Aayog, set up 18 September 2015 by merging PEO and IEO; monitors and evaluates government programmes.

08-004.r: NDC (1952) was parallel to, not an organ of, Planning Commission; Economic and Social Planning → Concurrent List; Constitution asks Panchayats to plan for economic development and social justice.
08-004.t: NDC is not a part of the Planning Commission; NITI Aayog's Governing Council now does NDC's role.

08-006.r: Finance Commission (constitutional) → reviews revenue segment of budget; Planning Commission (non-constitutional) → reviewed both capital and revenue needs of States.
08-006.t: Finance Commission is constitutional; Planning Commission was not.

08-007.r: Ashok Chandra called the Planning Commission the 'Economic Cabinet of India' (undefined position, wide terms of reference).

08-008.r: National Development Council (6 August 1952), chaired by Prime Minister → reviewed and approved Five Year Plans drafted by Planning Commission.
08-008.t: Planning Commission drafted the Plan; NDC approved it.

08-015.r: Planning Commission → set up March 1950 by Cabinet Resolution; advisory, non-constitutional body (also called quasi-political).

08-019.r: Wrong: NITI Aayog has a full-time Chairman → PM is ex-officio Chairperson, with full-time Vice Chairman; set up 1 January 2015 replacing Planning Commission; cooperative federalism.

08-020.r: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) → 1 January 2015, by Cabinet Resolution, replacing Planning Commission; a public policy think tank.
08-020.h: NITI Aayog was born on New Year's Day 2015.

08-025.r: Nodal institution for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in India → NITI Aayog.

08-026.r: First Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog → Arvind Panagariya (January 2015 to August 2017); Suman Bery since 1 May 2022.

08-027.r: NITI Aayog CEOs → Sindhushree Khullar, then Amitabh Kant (second, from 17 February 2016), now B.V.R. Subrahmanyam (from 25 February 2023).

08-028.r: India Innovation Index 2019 (NITI Aayog, October 17, 2019) → Karnataka top among major States; kept top spot in 2020 and 2021 editions.

08-029.r: NITI Aayog report → Bihar fastest growing State economy in 2014-15; MoSPI: Manipur highest GSDP growth (13.51%) in 2021-22.

08-030.r: NITI Aayog State Health Index 2019 (second edition, June 2019) → Bihar scored 32.11; Kerala topped fourth edition (2019-20) at 82.20.

08-031.r: Planning Commission → not mentioned in Constitution; no fixed tenure for Deputy Chairman and members; no fixed qualification for members.

08-032.r: Planning Commission Deputy Chairmen → Manmohan Singh (1985–1987), Pranab Mukherjee (1991–1996), Montek Singh Ahluwalia (2004–2014); P. Chidambaram never held it.

08-033.r: Prime Minister → ex-officio Chairman of Planning Commission; A.M. Khusro, N.K.P. Salve, M.S. Ahluwalia never Chairman (Ahluwalia was Deputy Chairman 2004–2014).
08-033.t: Don't confuse Chairman (PM, ex-officio) with Deputy Chairman (nominated, e.g. Montek Singh Ahluwalia).

08-035.r: Linked to Planning → National Development Council (approved Plans) and Parliament (Plan presented after NDC approval); not Finance Commission or Ministries.

08-036.r: 'India Vision 2020' → committee under Dr. S.P. Gupta, Planning Commission member, set up June 2000; stressed employment and education.

08-037.r: Planning needed for → balanced socio-economic development, even spread of benefits, removing regional disparities, maximum use of resources (all four).

08-038.r: Imperative planning → market replaced by central command; indicative planning → state indicates direction and supports the market.
08-038.h: Imperative = orders (command); Indicative = indicates (guides the market).

08-039.r: Largest source for India's plan public expenditure → borrowings (G-Secs, treasury bills, external assistance, small savings securities).

08-040.r: Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula (Central Plan Assistance from 8th Plan, 1992-97) → population (1971) 60 percent; per capita income 25; special problems 7.5.
08-040.h: 60-25-7.5-7.5: population, per capita income, performance, special problems.

08-041.r: National Planning Committee → set up October 1938 by Congress President Subhash Chandra Bose; Jawaharlal Nehru was its Chairman.
08-041.t: Set up by Bose, chaired by Nehru; don't pick Nehru as founder.

08-042.r: Wardha, August 1937 → Congress Working Committee resolution on national reconstruction and social planning; Bose's Haripura speech backed a planning commission scheme.

08-043.r: Gandhian Plan (1944) → Shriman Narayan Agarwal; small-unit production, agriculture, decentralisation, self-contained villages, cottage industries.

08-045.r: Mahatma Gandhi opposed planned development; he favoured simple living, self-sufficiency, local resources and local labour for local needs.

08-046.r: Sarvodaya Plan (1950) → Jayaprakash Narayan, on Gandhian ideals; from 1954 he devoted himself to the Sarvodaya Movement.
08-046.t: Don't confuse Sarvodaya Plan (Jayaprakash Narayan) with Gandhian Plan (Shriman Narayan Agarwal).

08-047.r: Rolling Plan (Gunnar Myrdal) → three plans: current-year plan with budget; plan of 3-5 years revised every year; perspective plan of 10-20 years.
08-047.h: A Rolling Plan 'rolls forward' one year at a time.

08-050.r: Rolling Plan in India → Janata Party Government, 1978-79, after rejecting Fifth Five Year Plan; flexible, revised yearly.

08-052.r: Major objective of Five Year Plans → self-reliance and less dependence on foreign aid; also higher living standards and employment.

08-053.r: Five Year Plan goals → growth, modernisation, self-reliance; 'literature' was never a goal, so answer is 'None of the above'.

08-054.r: 12th Five Year Plan → 2012-2017; theme 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'; 2016-17 was its last year.

08-057.r: 12th Plan targets → real GDP growth 8.0%, agriculture 4.0%, manufacturing 10.0%, poverty head-count cut by 10 percentage points; 50 million non-farm jobs.
08-057.c: Book gives no single answer: all three are 12th Plan targets, so none is 'not a vision', and (d) 'All of the above' fails too.

08-058.r: 12th Plan target growth for agriculture, forestry and fisheries → 4.0 percent a year.

08-060.r: 12th Plan vision paper → 9 percent GDP growth target; NDC fixed it at 8 percent (December 2012) when approving the Plan.
08-060.t: Don't confuse 9% (vision paper) with 8% (final NDC target).

08-061.r: 12th Plan largest allocation → Social Services (2664843 crore, about 34.7 percent of outlay); Energy 18.8 percent.

08-063.r: 12th Plan infrastructure investment need → Rs. 55.7 lakh crore (about US $1000 billion).

08-064.r: 12th Plan (2012-17) → 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'; 11th Plan (2007-12) → 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'.
08-064.h: 12th Plan adds 'Sustainable' to the 11th Plan's theme.

08-067.r: 11th Five Year Plan (2007-12) → 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'.
08-067.t: Don't confuse with 12th Plan's 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'.

08-073.r: 11th Plan Approach Paper → with target growth and 1.5 percent population growth, average Indian's real income doubles in ten years.

08-074.r: 11th Plan → biggest expected job growth in construction (8.27%); transport and communication 7.6%; manufacturing and agriculture 4% each.

08-075.r: Eleventh Plan total outlay → Rs. 36,44,718 crore; 12th Plan outlay → Rs. 76,69,807 crore.

08-076.r: 11th Plan highest allocation → social services, then energy sector; among the options, energy.

08-077.r: 11th Plan → social sector had maximum combined Central, State and UT expenditure.

08-078.r: 11th Plan targets → GDP 9%; agriculture 4% (double the 10th Plan's 2%); industry 10.5 percent (10% to 11%, up from 9.2%).

08-080.r: 11th Plan GDP growth target → 9.0 percent a year; achieved 8.0 percent.

08-081.r: Eleventh Plan inclusive growth → reduce poverty, expand employment, reduce gender inequality; strengthening capital market not included.

08-082.r: 11th Plan education theme → compulsory elementary education; aim to cut elementary drop-out rate from 52.2% (2003-2004) to 20% by 2011-12.

08-083.r: 11th Plan (2007 to 2012), endorsed by NDC → eight new IITs to be set up.

08-084.r: 10th Plan (2002-07) → growth target 8 percent; cut to 7 percent in mid-term appraisal; actual 7.6 percent.
08-084.t: Don't confuse original target (8%) with mid-term appraisal figure (7%).

08-086.r: 10th Five Year Plan → 1 April 2002 to 31 March 2007; ended in 2007.

08-088.r: 10th Plan targets → 8% GDP growth; poverty ratio down 5 points to about 20% by 2007; literacy 75% (not 73%).

08-089.r: Tenth Plan outlay → Energy highest (26.47%); Social services 22.79%; Transport 14.31%; Communication 6.43%.

08-090.r: Tenth Plan highest target growth → communication (15%); financial services 11.69%; manufacturing 9.82%; trade 9.44%; agriculture 3.97%.

08-091.r: Tenth Plan crop growth → pulses and oilseeds highest (4.29%); other crops 3.58%; fruits and vegetables 2.97%; cereals 1.28%.

08-092.r: Tenth Plan → investment rate (32.10% of GDP) was higher than domestic savings rate (26.84%).

08-093.r: GDP growth in 2000-02 → only about half of the Tenth Plan target.

08-094.r: 9th Plan (1997-2002), United Front Government → 'Growth with Social Justice and Equity'.

08-095.r: 9th Plan → growth target 6.5 percent; actual 5.4 percent; theme 'Growth with Social Justice and Equity'.

08-096.r: 9th Plan → 57.1 percent of education budget for primary education (nearest option 58%).

08-097.r: Women's Component Plan → entered in 7th Plan (27 women's schemes monitored); major strategy in 9th Plan (1997-2002): not less than 30 percent funds for women.

08-098.r: 9th Plan (1997-2002) → Incremental Capital-Output Ratio (ICOR) 4.3 (nearest option 4.0); savings 26.1% and investment 28.2% of GDP.

08-099.r: 7th Plan ended 31 March 1990; 1990-91 and 1991-92 were Annual Plans; 8th Plan ran April 1992 to March 1997.

08-101.r: 8th Plan → recognised 'human development' as core of all development efforts; aimed at near-full employment.

08-102.r: Human Resource Development focus → 8th Plan (employment, education, public health); not Fifth, First or Third, so 'None of the above'.

08-103.r: 8th Plan (1992-97), delayed two years → target growth 5.6 percent; actual 6.8 percent.

08-104.r: 8th Plan targets → GDP growth 5.6 percent; industrial growth 7.5 percent.

08-105.r: 8th Plan → national investment Rs. 798000 crore; public sector outlay Rs. 434100 crore; growth target 5.6% a year.

08-106.r: 8th Plan public sector outlay (Rs. 434100 crore) → largest source government borrowings (Rs. 202255 crore, 46.6%).

08-107.r: 8th Plan's major shift → public investment concentrated in infrastructure sectors; more scope for private sector amid reforms.

08-109.r: Shift from heavy industries to infrastructure → 8th Plan (1992-97), with liberalisation under PM P.V. Narsimha Rao; growth 6.8% vs 5.6% target.

08-111.r: 7th Plan (1985-90) slogan → 'Food, Work and Productivity'; achieved 6% growth against 5% target.

08-113.r: IRDP (launched 2 October 1980 in all blocks) → 'total household approach' adopted as strategy in 7th Plan.
hi: Integrated Rural Development Programme (समन्वित ग्रामीण विकास कार्यक्रम)

08-114.r: IRDP → launched 2 October 1980 in 6th Plan (1980 to 1985); subsidy plus bank credit for rural poor; merged into Swarna Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojna April 1999.

08-115.r: Rolling Plan → Janata Party's Sixth Plan (1978) after ending Fifth Plan; ended 1979; Congress then ran new Sixth Plan 1980-85.

08-116.r: Fifth Plan (scheduled 1974-79) → Emergency 1975, elections, Janata Party win; ended 1978, one year early; final draft by D.P. Dhar.

08-118.r: Fifth Plan → twin aims: removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance (zero net foreign aid).

08-120.r: 'Garibi Hatao' → Indira Gandhi's 1971 election slogan, during 4th Plan (1969-74); poverty removal became main objective of 5th Plan (UPPSC answer: 5th Plan).
08-120.c: Book gives no single answer: by the 1971 'Garibi Hatao' slogan it is the 4th Plan (b); by main objective it is the 5th Plan (c), which UPPSC accepted.

08-122.r: Chronology → Green Revolution (1966-67, HYV seeds) → Bank nationalisation (1969, 14 banks) → Garibi Hatao (Fifth Plan, 1974-79).

08-123.r: Growth Centre Approach → introduced in 4th Plan (1969-74) to remove regional disparities; special emphasis in 5th Plan.

08-124.r: Self-sustaining development first adopted in 4th Plan → twin aims 'growth with stability' and 'progressive achievement of self-reliance'.

08-125.r: Socialistic pattern of society → 2nd Plan (1956-61), on P.C. Mahalanobis model; rapid industrialisation with heavy and basic industries.
08-125.h: Second Plan is also called the 'Mahalanobis Plan'.
hi: Socialistic pattern of society (समाजवादी समाज का ढांचा)

08-128.r: Architect of Indian planning → P.C. Mahalanobis; real planning began with 2nd Plan (1956-61), built on his ideas.

08-129.r: Mahalanobis model (2nd Plan, 1956-61) → rapid industrialisation through capital-intensive heavy and basic industries; agriculture lower priority.

08-131.r: 2nd Five Year Plan → maximum emphasis on industrial sector (capital-intensive heavy and basic industries).

08-132.r: First Five Year Plan → began 1 April 1951 (1951-52); earlier ideas: National Planning Committee 1938, Bombay and Gandhian Plans 1944, People's Plan 1945.

08-134.r: First Five Year Plan (1951) → based on Harrod-Domar model; focus on primary sector.
08-134.t: Don't confuse: First Plan → Harrod-Domar; Second Plan → Mahalanobis.

08-135.r: First Plan (1951-56) → priority agriculture; Harrod-Domar model; succeeded due to good harvests.

08-136.r: 2nd Plan → heavy industries (true); import substitution began with 2nd Plan in 1950s, not 3rd Plan (false).

08-137.r: True: 2nd Plan → thrust on substituting basic and capital goods; 4th Plan → correct concentration of wealth and power. False: financial sector part of 5th Plan.

08-138.r: Plan models → 1st Harrod-Domar; 2nd Mahalanobis; 3rd S. Chakravarty; 4th Ashok Rudra.
08-138.h: HMCR (Plans 1 to 4): 'Hard Men Climb Rocks' = Harrod-Domar, Mahalanobis, Chakravarty, Rudra.

08-139.r: 1st Plan → Community Development (1952); 2nd → rapid industrialisation; 3rd → basic industries; 4th → self-reliance, growth with stability; 5th → Minimum Needs Programme.

08-141.r: Highest actual growth among options → Tenth Plan (7.6%); First 3.6%, Fourth 3.3%, Sixth 5.7%; Eleventh Plan (8.0%) highest overall.

08-142.r: Highest real GNP growth among the Fifth to Eighth Plans → Eighth Five Year Plan.

08-143.r: Highest growth among Seventh to Tenth Plans → Tenth Plan; across all Plans, the Eleventh Plan recorded the highest growth.

08-145.r: Maximum per capita growth → Eleventh Plan; with 9% GDP target, per capita GDP to grow about 7.6% a year, doubling in under ten years.

08-146.r: U.P. growth rates → 6th Plan 3.9%; 7th Plan 5.7%; 8th Plan 3.2%; 9th Plan 2.5%.

08-147.r: Seven years with no Five Year Plan → 1966-69 (three Annual Plans), Rolling Plan 1978-79, 1979-80, Annual Plans 1990-92.

08-148.r: Plan Holiday → 1 April 1966 to 31 March 1969 (three Annual Plans) between 3rd and 4th Plans.

08-150.r: Decade of jobless growth → 1991-2000; organised sector job growth 0.36% vs 2.6% target in early 8th Plan; employment growth fell to about 1%.

08-151.r: Twenty Point Programme → launched 1975; revised 1982 and 1986; restructured 2006; aim: poverty eradication and better quality of life.

08-152.r: Core sector → selected basic industries: electricity, steel, refinery products, crude oil, coal, cement, natural gas, fertilizers.

08-153.r: Planning continued after 1991 market reforms → Five Year Plans gave long-term perspective in market-friendly way; 12th Plan (2012-17) was the last.

08-154.r: Industrial planning declined in the nineties (private sector, market role, focus on HRD and infrastructure); untrue: priorities shifted from industry to rural development.

08-155.r: 'Bottom-Up Planning' still a goal; village is the basic planning unit (Article 40, DPSP); 73rd Amendment, 1993 embodied Panchayati Raj.

08-156.r: Chronology → India joined IMF (1945) → first rupee devaluation (1949) → First Plan to Parliament (8 December 1951) → NDC set up (6 August 1952).
08-156.h: 'I Did Plan Next': IMF, Devaluation, Plan, NDC.

08-157.r: 'Yojana' monthly → Publications Division, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; started 1957, first Chief Editor Khuswant Singh.

08-158.r: 'Planned Economy for India' → M. Visvesvaraya, first to advocate planning; proposed a ten-year plan to double national income through industrialisation.
